• finite Hecke generators 𝑇𝑠 for each simple reflection 𝑠 ∈ 𝑊0 , satisfying the braid and quadratic (𝑇𝑠 −
  𝑞 )(𝑇𝑠 + 1) = 0 relations.
The interaction between the two layers is the Bernstein relation: for a simple reflection 𝑠 = 𝑠 𝛼 with simple

ture to a coherent-sheaf convolution on the Steinberg variety; it is the categorical lift of the Bernstein
presentation, and the chapter’s framing "Bezrukavnikov–Bernstein–Langlands" records the three layers.

16.8    The Arithmetic Langlands Diamond for V prim
   (i) Bun𝐺 𝐿2 (Spec ℤ) ≃ 𝐵𝐺 𝐿2 (ℤ) has one coarse point and nontrivial stabilizer (Chapter 16.1.2); it
       is too small geometrically to carry the required Hecke correspondence, forcing the passage to the
       Iwahori-equivariant setting.
  (ii) The spherical Hecke algebra is commutative (Satake isomorphism); the Iwahori-equivariant affine
       Hecke category HkIw  𝐺 𝐿2 , 𝑝 carries the noncommutative convolution datum (Chapter 16.3.1).
 (iii) The spectral side is the Selmer-derived global stack, built from local Emerton–Gee/( 𝜑, Γ) stacks
       with fixed residual representation, determinant, and local conditions.
 (iv) Arithmetic Arinkin–Gaitsgory: Fargues–Scholze and Emerton–Gee supply local inputs;
       the automorphic-to-IndCohNilp equivalence is conditional locally and conjectural globally
       (Chapter 16.4.2).
  (v) Crowning placement: V prim = HH• (HkIw         𝐺 𝐿2 ,glob ) (Chapter 16.5.1).
 (vi) Three-way comparison with Kim–Gaiotto arithmetic Chern–Simons and Costello–Gwilliam
       factorization (Chapter 16.6.1).
(vii) Hecke-trace tabulation recovers the Eichler–Selberg formula (Chapter 16.7.2).
    V prim is an arithmetic Hochschild character. It encodes on the automorphic side the universal trace
of the identity on the global Iwahori Hecke category of 𝐺 𝐿2 ; on the spectral side, through the conjectural
arithmetic Langlands equivalence, the structure sheaf O of the global Galois-deformation stack. The
rank-2 Heisenberg presentation per prime is the Whittaker model of this trace, with the two generators
diagonalising the Satake parameters.

Arithmetic 𝐸𝑛 Formality and CoHA

17.1   Rectification of the ordered product
The little-interval operad controls an ordered multiplication before passing to cohomology. Its integral
formality permits associative DGA models. Formality of a particular DGA asks for a further multiplica-
tive comparison with its cohomology.
Theorem 17.1.1 (integral formality of the little-interval operad). For every commutative ring 𝑆 ,
the component augmentation gives an operadic quasi-isomorphism

                                           𝐶• ( 𝐸1 ; 𝑆 ) −→ Ass 𝑆 .

Here Ass 𝑆 ( 𝑛) = 𝑆 [ Σ𝑛 ] records the order of 𝑛 inputs.

Proof. Each component of the space of 𝑛 disjoint labeled intervals is specified by their left-to-right order.
For a fixed order, their endpoints satisfy linear inequalities. Their parameter space is convex and there-
fore contractible. There are 𝑛! components, freely permuted by Σ𝑛 . The singular-chain augmentation
maps every zero-simplex to its component and every positive-dimensional simplex to zero. It is a quasi-
isomorphism in each arity. Substitution of intervals substitutes their input orders, so these maps respect
operadic composition and units.

Corollary 17.1.2 (rectification and cohomology). Whenever the operadic change-of-algebra ad-
junction satisfies its rectification hypotheses, an ordered 𝐸1 -algebra has an associative DGA model. This
conclusion concerns its multiplication on chains. It supplies no quasi-isomorphism to its cohomology
algebra. The nonformal algebras of Theorem 17.5.3 are strict associative examples over ℤ.

Proof. Apply the rectification adjunction to the preceding operadic quasi-isomorphism. A DGA still
has its differential, and passage to cohomology requires a separate multiplicative quasi-isomorphism
zigzag. For the last assertion take 𝑆 = ℤ, 𝑐 = 2, and 𝑟 = 2 in Theorem 17.5.3.

17.2   An integral obstruction for the little-disk operad
The action of input permutations is part of a symmetric operad. It already distinguishes chains on two
little disks from their homology.
Theorem 17.2.1 (the arity-two obstruction). The chain operad 𝐶• ( 𝐸2 ; 𝑆 ) is not formal as a sym-
metric operad for 𝑆 = ℤ or 𝑆 = 𝔽 2 .

Proof. In arity two, the direction between the disk centres gives an equivariant homotopy equivalence
with 𝑆 1 . The transposition group 𝐺 = Σ2 acts by the antipodal map. This action is free and induces the
identity on both homology groups. Thus homology with zero differential is 𝑆 ⊕ 𝑆 [1] as a complex of
𝑆 [ 𝐺 ]-modules, in homological grading.


                                                     85
86                                                Chapter 17. Arithmetic 𝐸𝑛 Formality and CoHA


   Derived coinvariants of the actual chains compute 𝐻• ( 𝑆 1 /𝐺 ; 𝑆 ), since the action is free. They vanish
above degree one. Derived coinvariants of the zero-differential homology complex are

                                        𝐻• ( 𝐺 ; 𝑆 ) ⊕ 𝐻• ( 𝐺 ; 𝑆 ) [1] .

The periodic resolution for 𝐺 = ⟨ 𝑔 : 𝑔 2 = 1⟩ has alternating maps 1 − 𝑔 and 1 + 𝑔 . On the trivial
module they become 0 and 2. For 𝑆 = ℤ, this gives a nonzero ℤ/2 in every positive odd degree. For
𝑆 = 𝔽 2 , it gives a nonzero group in every degree. Hence the two derived coinvariant complexes cannot
be quasi-isomorphic. An operadic formality zigzag would give such an equivalence already in arity two,
which is impossible.

Corollary 17.2.2 (coefficient and operad choices). The integral chain operad cannot be replaced
by Gerℤ through a symmetric-operad formality zigzag. Integral 𝐸2 -algebras can nevertheless exist. Over
ℚ, Tamarkin’s formality theorem supplies a formality comparison for the operad, with a choice of such
comparison (Tamarkin, Formality of chain operad of little discs, Lett. Math. Phys. 66 (2003), Theorem 2.1,
p. 67). This operadic comparison does not make every individual algebra formal.

Proof. The integral assertion follows from the preceding theorem, since 𝐻• ( 𝐸2 ; ℤ) = Gerℤ . An algebra
over the chain operad requires an operad action, which does not require formality of the acting operad.
For example, an ordinary commutative algebra is an algebra over that operad through its augmentation
to the commutative operad. The rational assertion is the cited operadic theorem. Its change-of-operad
construction retains the differential of each algebra.

Remark 17.2.3 (obstructions under coeﬃcient change). The class of a higher multiplication belongs to
a specified Hochschild cochain complex. Comparing such classes after coefficient change requires a
comparison of those complexes. For the explicit family below, monic division supplies this comparison
on the chosen minimal structure. Its obstruction is detected directly in 𝑆 /𝑐 𝑆 by Theorem 17.5.3. No
quotient of unrelated Hochschild cohomology groups is used.

17.3   Strict operations and transferred operations
Let 𝐷ord be an associative DGA representing an ordered arithmetic factorization algebra, when that
representation has been constructed. Its differential and product are its operations on chains. The
Hochschild trace class V prim remains a separate object until a comparison with that algebra is specified.
Theorem 17.3.1 (operations in a strict model). Every associative DGA 𝐷ord defines an 𝐴∞ -algebra
with 𝑚1 = 𝑑 , 𝑚2 its product, and 𝑚𝑘 = 0 for 𝑘 ≥ 3. Its transferred operations on cohomology need not
vanish.

Proof. The arity-one identity is 𝑑 2 = 0. The arity-two identity is the Leibniz rule, and the arity-three
identity is associativity. Every higher identity has zero terms. The transfer calculation in Lemma 17.5.1
gives 𝑚4 = −𝑢𝐹 ⌣ 𝐹 on cohomology of a strict DGA. Its nonzero obstruction class for a nonunit
parameter is proved in Theorem 17.5.3.

Corollary 17.3.2 (the two formality questions). A strict integral model can have a nonformal
minimal model on its cohomology. Therefore the vanishing of its displayed chain operations for 𝑘 ≥ 3
does not remove higher-operation obstructions to arithmetic centre comparisons.

Proof. The model 𝐴 (ℤ, 2, 2) has precisely these properties by Theorem 17.5.3.

Corollary 17.8.1 (the exceptional coefficient). For 𝑟 ≥ 2, the nonpositive part of the integral
relative centre is nonformal. Its extension from ℤ to 𝑆 is formal exactly when 2 ∈ 𝑆 × . In particular it is
formal over ℚ and every field of odd characteristic, and nonformal over every field of characteristic two
and over ℤ/4. The full 𝐶𝑆,𝑟 is nonformal whenever 2 is a nonunit in 𝑆 and 𝑟 ≥ 2. For 𝑟 = 1, both the
full centre and its nonpositive part are formal over every 𝑆 .

Proof. The assertions about the nonpositive part follow from Proposition 17.4.2 and Theorem 17.5.3.
For any cochain DGA 𝐷 , the complex with 𝐷 𝑛 in negative degrees, 𝑍 0 ( 𝐷 ) in degree zero, and zero in
positive degrees is a sub-DGA. This truncation functor preserves quasi-isomorphisms. Applying it to a
formality zigzag for 𝐶𝑆,𝑟 would give a formality zigzag for 𝐴 ( 𝑆, 2, 𝑟 ). This proves the stated nonformality
of the full centre. For 𝑟 = 1, the inclusion 𝑆 [ 𝑢, 𝑧 ]/( 𝑧 2 ) ↩→ 𝐶𝑆,1 is a quasi-isomorphism: monic division
identifies cohomology by substituting 𝑡 = 2𝑢𝑧 . The analogous inclusion of 𝐵 proves the nonpositive
assertion.

Example 17.8.3 (unit and nonunit parameters). For 𝑆 = 𝔽 2 and 𝑟 = 2, the model 𝐴 ( 𝑆, 0, 2) has
𝑚4 ( 𝑡, 𝑡, 𝑡, 𝑡 ) = −𝑢 = 𝑢 and is nonformal. The model 𝐴 ( 𝑆, 1, 2) is formal by the explicit zigzag. It is
not the reduction of 𝐴 (ℤ, 2, 2), whose parameter reduces to zero. Over ℤ/4, the parameters 2 and 3
likewise give nonformal and formal models, respectively. The criterion is invertibility of 𝑐 , rather than its
nonvanishing. For the zero ring, the unique element is a unit and every displayed algebra is zero.
    The global arithmetic object V prim of Definition 16.3.2 is a Hochschild trace class. The centre above
is a relative derived endomorphism algebra. A comparison between them requires a multiplicative map
with a specified base, source, target, and cohomology isomorphism. An equality of degree-zero centres
does not supply these data.
Proposition 17.8.4 (scope of the centre obstruction). Let Z be an associative 𝑆 -DGA model
for an arithmetic derived centre. Suppose a finite multiplicative 𝑆 -linear quasi-isomorphism zigzag
identifies 𝜏≤0 Z with 𝐴 ( 𝑆, 2, 𝑟 ). If 𝑟 ≥ 2 and 2 is a nonunit, then Z is nonformal over 𝑆 . If the full Z

of the required identification.

Proof. A formality zigzag for Z would truncate to one for 𝜏≤0 Z. Composing with the hypothesized
comparison would make 𝐴 ( 𝑆, 2, 𝑟 ) formal, contrary to Theorem 17.5.3. The full comparison transfers
the classification in Theorem 17.7.2.

   The positive zigzag fixes 𝑆 [ 𝑡, 𝑢] on the nonpositive algebra. The full centre has the additional sixth-
operation obstruction of Theorem 17.7.2. For the global Iwahori category, the required relative bimodule
comparison is an additional construction, independent of rectification of the 𝐸1 operad.

17.9    The Chiral Bracket via Adelic Residue
Deﬁnition 17.9.1 (archimedean 𝜆-bracket on the cover). Let 𝐶 denote the Arakelov compactification of the
arithmetic curve, obtained by adjoining the archimedean place | · | ∞ to Spec ℤ. The Beilinson–Drinfeld
𝜆-bracket is defined only on the archimedean Heisenberg cover, where a holomorphic diagonal and a
complex residue exist:
                                    { 𝑎, 𝑏 }∞ = Res 𝑧 =𝑤 𝜔 𝑎,𝑏 ( 𝑧, 𝑤 ) .
No finite prime contributes a vertex-algebra residue on V prim . A finite-place bracket would require a
separate prismatic construction and is not part of the Hochschild trace class.
Theorem 17.9.2 (finite-place residue obstruction). The archimedean bracket above does not de-
scend to a Beilinson–Drinfeld bracket on V prim over 𝐶 . Finite places are totally disconnected in the
factorization topology used here, and the global object is an 𝐸1 Hochschild trace class rather than a vertex
algebra.

Proposition 17.11.4 (the multiplicative PBW criterion). The map (17.9) is an algebra isomor-
phism if and only if the embedded generators 𝜄 (𝑈 ) pairwise supercommute in H 𝜓 . An ordinary poly-
nomial algebra on these homogeneous generators additionally requires 𝑈 to have no odd part.

Proof. If the generators supercommute, the universal property gives an algebra map from Symsup (𝑈 )
to H 𝜓 . On a product of 𝑛 generators it equals the signed average of the 𝑛! ordered Hall products, hence
equals the PBW map and is bijective. Conversely, an algebra map extending 𝜄 preserves the defining
supercommutation relations. Over ℚ a nonzero odd generator in the symmetric superalgebra has square
zero, whereas an ordinary polynomial algebra over ℚ is reduced.

17.12    Cyclic potentials and the arithmetic comparison
The logarithmic Euler series does have a cyclic realization, but its critical locus tests whether it can serve
as a Hall potential. For an associative algebra 𝐴, degree-zero cyclic homology is HC0 ( 𝐴) = 𝐴/[ 𝐴, 𝐴] vect .
Over a field, degree-zero cyclic cohomology consists of linear traces 𝜆 : 𝐴 → 𝐾 satisfying 𝜆 ( 𝑎𝑏 ) =
𝜆 ( 𝑏𝑎). These constructions neither adjoin coefficients nor supply a map from an arbitrary Dirichlet
series into a path algebra.

to a single generator per prime needs a specified subalgebra or quotient, as in (17.7).

trace remains open. The prime Fock trace proves the Euler product on an explicit carrier; the zero-loop
calculation excludes an edgeless CoHA on a nonempty prime set as that carrier; the logarithmic-potential
calculation excludes its most direct completed critical realization; and the tripled- 𝐴2 calculation shows
why a PBW theorem alone cannot remove the multiplication obstruction.

17.13   Arithmetic Formality Stratification
The operadic statements concern the chains on little intervals and little disks. The little-interval operad
is formal over ℤ by Theorem 17.1.1. The little-disk operad has the integral arity-two obstruction of
Theorem 17.2.1. For an individual associative DGA, the multiplication on cohomology has its own
obstruction classes. The explicit coefficient criterion is Theorem 17.5.3. Its centre interpretation uses the
relative bimodule model and truncation map of Proposition 17.4.1 and Proposition 17.4.2. An application
to the global arithmetic centre requires the multiplicative comparison specified in Proposition 17.8.4. The
archimedean residue bracket uses the separate geometric data in Definition 17.9.1. The Euler product is
realized by the prime-monoid Hilbert space in Proposition 17.10.3 and by the degree-zero Jordan-CoHA
sector in (17.7). An identification with BPS cohomology requires the graded realization and compatible
maps of Proposition 17.12.2. The perverse PBW theorem supplies the underlying graded object; its
multiplicative refinement requires vanishing Hall supercommutators.
Chapter 18


The Arithmetic Yangian Collapses to Its Bethe
Subalgebra

The Yangian 𝑌 (𝔤𝔩 𝑛 ) is controlled by the RTT presentation, an 𝑅-matrix, and a spectral parameter. An
arithmetic Yangian has no uniform spectral difference 𝑢 − 𝑣 across primes. The surviving structure is
the commutative Bethe algebra together with the automorphic modularity condition.
    The Yangian 𝑌 (𝔤𝔩 𝑛 ) (Drinfeld 1985, 1988) is a Hopf algebra deformation of 𝑈 (𝔤𝔩 𝑛 [ 𝑧 ]) defined by
the RTT relation 𝑅 ( 𝑢 − 𝑣 ) (𝑇 ( 𝑢) ⊗ 1) (1 ⊗ 𝑇 ( 𝑣 )) = (1 ⊗ 𝑇 ( 𝑣 )) (𝑇 ( 𝑢) ⊗ 1) 𝑅 ( 𝑢 − 𝑣 ) with Yang’s
rational 𝑅-matrix 𝑅 ( 𝑢) = 1 + 𝑃 /𝑢 (here 𝑃 the permutation operator on 𝑉 ⊗ 𝑉 ). The question is
whether this structure admits an arithmetic analogue over Spec ℤ. Four independent obstructions show
it does not. The correct arithmetic replacement is the commutative Bethe subalgebra, whose spectrum
is the automorphic spectrum of 𝐺 𝐿𝑛 .

18.1   The Four Obstructions to a Naive Arithmetic Yangian
Theorem 18.1.1 (four structural obstructions to the RTT model). . Yang’s additive RTT construc-
tion with 𝑅-matrix 𝑅 ( 𝑢) = 1 + 𝑃 /𝑢 has no arithmetic analogue satisfying the four requirements below:
   (i) Discrete-continuous mismatch. The spectral parameter 𝑢 is continuous and Spec ℤ is discrete;
       primes cannot be spectral parameters.
  (ii) No cross-prime subtraction. 𝑢 − 𝑣 has no analogue across distinct primes (ℚ 𝑝 ̸↩→ ℚ𝑞 for
       𝑝 ≠ 𝑞 ).
 (iii) No meromorphic 1-form on Spec ℤ. Costello 4D Chern–Simons (arXiv:1709.09993) requires a
       meromorphic 1-form 𝜔 on the spectral-parameter direction; Spec ℤ has none.
 (iv) No 𝜁 -valued shuffle kernel. Arithmetic shuffle-kernel constructions with 𝜁 -valued kernels fail
       the cocycle condition (Feigin–Odesskii).
Corollary 18.1.2 (no RTT arithmetic Yangian as Hopf algebra). . 𝑌 arith (𝔤𝔩 𝑛 ) does not exist as
a noncommutative Hopf algebra deforming 𝑈 (𝔤𝔩 𝑛 [ 𝑧 ]) with the specified additive spectral parameter,
arithmetic 𝑅-matrix, and RTT relation. Other categorical or non-RTT notions are not excluded by this
obstruction.

18.2   The Bethe-Algebra Collapse
The four obstructions force the question: what commutative quotient of the Yangian does admit an
arithmetic analogue? The answer is the Bethe subalgebra, which over ℂ is already the coordinate ring of
opers on a disk.

18.3   Primes Are Lattice Sites, Not Spectral Parameters
Principle 18.3.1 (site-spectral duality). In the XXZ spin chain from 𝑈𝑞 (𝔰𝔩
                                                                         b 2 ), sites are discrete (labelled
by ℤ or by particle number 𝑁 ); spectral parameter 𝑢 is continuous (∈ ℂ). Hecke eigenvalues live in ℂ
(spectral); primes live in ℤ ≥2 (site).
Corollary 18.3.2 (arithmetic spectral parameter is 𝑠 ). . The arithmetic spectral parameter is the
Langlands 𝑠 ∈ ℂ, not a prime, not a 𝑝-adic number. The spectral direction is the archimedean fibre ℂ∞ ;
the site direction is the Arakelov-compactified arithmetic curve Spec ℤ.
Heuristic 18.3.3 (4D Chern–Simons analogy, conditional on F2). . Costello–Witten–Yamazaki 4D CS
(arXiv:1709.09993) is a theory on Σ × 𝐶 with Σ a topological real 2-manifold and 𝐶 a complex curve
carrying a meromorphic 1-form; its factorization algebra lives on Σ. The direct identification Σ = Spec ℤ
is dimensionally inconsistent on two counts. (i) Spec ℤ has étale cohomological dimension 3 (Artin–
Verdier duality), not 2, so Spec ℤ × ℂ has total real dimension 5, not 4. (ii) Each finite place of Spec ℤ
carries only locally constant ( 𝐸0 ) factorization structure (Chapter 8.4.1), so a 2-dimensional 𝐸1 -chiral
factorization algebra of 4D CS type cannot live on the finite places at all; the 𝐸1 -chiral OPE concentrates
at the archimedean fibre ℂ∞ .
Remark 18.3.4 (rerouting the 4D CS analogy through F2). The honest analogy is conditional on Con-
jecture F2 (Chapter 20.2.1, perfectoid 𝐸2 -enhancement via Scholze diamonds). If F2 holds globally, the
diamond side of the global Iwahori Hecke supplies an étale 2-site 𝑆 ét with the Frobenius-semilinear
arithmetic-complex datum of Chapter 37.1.2, and the CWY identification becomes

         𝐶 = ℂ (spectral, 𝑠 -plane) ,        Σ = 𝑆 ét (Scholze-diamond 2-site, not Spec ℤ itself) ,
with the 𝐸1 -chiral OPE constructed at ℂ∞ and extended across 𝑆 ét by the F2 𝐸2 -monoidal structure
(Dunn additivity 𝐸1 ⊗ 𝐸1 = 𝐸2 ). Without F2 the 4D CS analogy is pattern-match only. The paral-
lel 3D analogy with Kim arithmetic Chern–Simons (arXiv:1510.05818) matches Spec ℤ dimensionally
but carries no spectral direction, and is the source of the five-presentation item (i) in the manifesto
(Chapter 2.1).

comparison below.

Remark 19.6.5 (honest domain restrictions). Three domain restrictions of the programme are carried by
the aCFT definition rather than hidden:
   (i) F2-conditional base. Item (B) assumes the Scholze-diamond 𝐸2 -enhancement. Without F2 the

       degenerates to a disjoint union of local aCFTs plus an archimedean aCFT.
  (ii) Admissible logarithmic lane (Creutzig–Kanade–Linshaw). Non-unitary admissible parameters
       are excluded from (M) and treated as a boundary of the aCFT category, not as elements of it.
 (iii) Super Bethe-Hecke chain-level coproduct (FM230). Outside the primary datum. Any super-
       enhancement of the aCFT must avoid RTT/Yangian claims and waits on an independent con-
       struction.
The aCFT of Chapter 19.6.1 is stated on the non-degenerate, non-admissible, non-super locus of the
programme.
Remark 19.6.6 (why this is a conformal ﬁeld theory). The five classical CFT data are present in direct
correspondence: (B) Riemann-surface base → arithmetic 𝑆 ét ; (V) vertex/chiral algebra → arithmetic
factorization algebra; (M) primary modules → local Hecke modules at each place; (F) conformal blocks
→ Tate integrals; (K) modular invariance → functional equation. What breaks from the classical picture
is the archimedean-only locus of 𝐸1 -chiral structure (finite places are 𝐸0 per (F1)–(F5)): the aCFT is a
stratiﬁed CFT, chiral at ∞ and locally constant elsewhere, rather than uniformly chiral.

19.7    Langlands as Arithmetic Bethe Ansatz
Theorem 19.7.1 (Drinfeld–solo). . The classical Jacquet–Langlands correspondence admits the
following Bethe/Hecke reading:
• Hecke eigenforms = Bethe eigenvectors of B arith ( 𝐺 𝐿𝑛 );
• Hecke eigenvalues = Bethe roots;
• Ramanujan–Petersson bound = Bethe-root unitarity;
• Automorphic spectral decomposition of 𝐿 2 ( 𝐺 𝐿𝑛 (𝔸)/𝐺 𝐿𝑛 (ℚ)) = diagonalisation of the transfer
  matrix on V prim ;
• modularity of 𝜌 supplies global Bethe-spectrum coherence; no RTT closure is asserted.
This is a heuristic dictionary, not a construction of an arithmetic RTT/Yangian Hopf algebra.

19.8    Source-Family Convergence
Remark 19.8.1 (common core of V prim ). (i) V prim is a Hochschild trace class with 𝐸1 -chiral structure
       at ∞ and 𝐸0 -locally constant structure at finite places. It carries no Virasoro action, no Beilinson–
       Drinfeld factorization on 𝐶 , and no Borger Λ-ring structure on the natural integral form.
  (ii) It is a spectral datum: Hochschild trace class, ACS boundary-shadow window, automorphic rep-
       resentation, Bethe algebra module.
 (iii) All arithmetic content lives on the Bost–Connes / automorphic / Hecke side; the VA structure
       that appears is the universal rank- 𝜋 ( 𝑁 ) Heisenberg descendant tower, which does not see the
       primes.
 (iv) Its finite-place scalar character is an 𝐿 -function: 𝜁 ( 𝑠 ) for the trivial sector or 𝐿 ( 𝑠, 𝜒 ) for Hecke
       characters 𝜒 , before archimedean completion.

19.10    Structural Rigidity of V prim
Theorem 19.10.1 (independence of surviving structure). . Every geometric enhancement of V prim
fails at a specific structural obstruction: the RTT/Yangian Hopf algebra fails by the absence of an arith-
metic 𝑅-matrix; Beilinson–Drinfeld factorization on 𝐶 fails by the non-uniform 𝐸1 / 𝐸0 stratification;
the Borger Λ-ring structure fails by the 𝜓 -ring vs Λ-ring obstruction (Gelfand–Borger source class). The
118                                            Chapter 19. Synthesis: Six Conditional Windows


Hochschild-trace candidate with six-window conditional synthesis and three open conjectures is the
maximal surviving structure; it is independent of which source comparison identifies it.
Remark 19.10.2 (Beilinson’s maximality principle). The surviving structure is structurally forced and
minimal: each deleted enhancement corresponds to a specific failed construction among the fifteen
constructions. The resulting core connects the Vol I chiral-bar-cobar programme to the arithmetic
Langlands tower at the Hochschild-trace level.

19.11   Logical Form of the Arithmetic Branch
The essential theorem (Chapter 19.2.1) holds unconditionally in its forward direction (Chapter 21.5.3);
the full equivalence is conditional on arithmetic Positselski and Koszul–Petersson compatibility
(Chapter 21.5.1). The six conditional windows (Chapter 19.1.1) are conjectures conditional on F1, F2, F3
(Chapter 19.9).
    Chapter 21 reduces F1, F2, F3 to five narrower residual conditions: LACD , F2.c, F3.BZNAr , arithmetic
Positselski, and Koszul–Petersson compatibility.
    Chapter 22 isolates the zero-placement clause of Conjecture F-RH (Chapter 22.1.1) as RH. The
full conjecture also contains the unitary arithmetic structure on V prim ; its zero-placement clause is re-
ducible to the arithmetic triangle: arithmetic Positselski, Koszul–Petersson compatibility, and arithmetic
Virasoro positivity VB∗ (Chapter 22.6.1).
Principle 19.11.1 (Courage, after Drinfeld). The equals sign 𝜅GAr + ( 𝜅 ! )GAr = 0 ⇔ 𝜉 ( 𝑠 ) = 𝜉 (1 − 𝑠 ) is
a theorem waiting to be stated. Arithmetic Koszul duality for the Heisenberg archetype, stated as an
equivalence between Vol I’s derived-centre complementarity and the Riemann functional equation. The
chiral-algebras programme (Beilinson–Drinfeld AMS 2004) built chiral algebras on curves over ℂ; the
arithmetic extension, on curves over Spec ℤ, is the content of this branch.
    V prim is not a vertex algebra. It is the Hochschild trace class of the identity on the arithmetic Hecke
category, which lives at the triple point of the Langlands diamond, the Ben-Zvi–Nadler CS-Hecke-trace
triangle, and the Beilinson–Drinfeld chiral formalism, all three extended arithmetically.

   Chapter 21 resolves the six-window trace into LACD , F2.c, F3.BZNAr , arith. Positselski, and Koszul–Pet
compatibility. The Riemann-Hypothesis branch of Chapter 22 is orthogonal to this trace construction except
where the explicit spectral positivity hypotheses are imposed.

Chapter 21


Closure of F1–F3 and Resolution of the Three
Pillars

The three conjectures F1, F2, F3 and the three pillars P1, P2, P3 record what the arithmetic branch requires
in order to complete the Riemann Hypothesis reformulation of Chapter 22. F1 asserts global categorical
arithmetic Langlands for 𝐺 𝐿2 /ℚ; F2 asserts that the global Hecke category is 𝐸2 -monoidal; F3 identifies
its Hochschild trace with V prim . P1 is the essential equivalence between 𝜅GAr + ( 𝜅 ! )GAr = 0 and the Tate
functional equation for Λ 𝜁 , equivalently for the pole-cleared 𝜉ℝ ; P2 is the Tate functional equation and
explicit formula; P3 is unitarity. Each conjecture and each pillar is subjected to the seven-obstruction crite-
rion below and either reduced to named components or proved conditionally. The residual obstructions
at the end of this chapter are precisely stated, independently testable claims.

21.1   Seven-Obstruction Reduction Criterion
A conjecture 𝐶 is a structured reduction of 𝐶0 if 𝐶0 ⇔ 𝐶 and 𝐶 is a conjunction of named inputs, each
of which is either a theorem in the literature, a conditional with identified literature gap, or a conjecture
with a precise statement. The seven obstructions are the structural tests for an equivalence claim. For
each condition they are:
   (i) Source separation. Are the proof source and the comparison source disjoint in the orthogonal
       sense?
  (ii) Sign / convention check. Do chain-level signs and 𝑞 -conventions match across cited sources?
 (iii) Ambient category check. Do LHS and RHS live in compatible ∞-categories?
 (iv) Missing hypothesis. Is a hidden hypothesis required (for instance sph-finiteness, perfectoid com-
       patibility, 𝜇 = 0)?
  (v) False functoriality. Does the claimed equivalence preserve all relevant structure?
 (vi) Unproved equivalence. Is any internal step itself a currently-open conjecture?
(vii) Numerical constant / numerical comparison. Do numerical-comparison checks rely on the same
       source as the derivation?
Each obstruction produces either a valid implication, a correction (reformulation that survives), or a
named residual obstruction. The result is a structured reduction, not necessarily a full closure.

21.2   F1: Structural Closure
Statement
F1 (Chapter 20.1.1) asserts

                               D( [ 𝐺 𝐿2 ]) sph-fin ≃ IndCohNilp X Sel
                                                                           
                                                                  ¯𝜌,det, L ,




                                                     125
126                      Chapter 21. Closure of F1–F3 and Resolution of the Three Pillars


the global categorical arithmetic Langlands equivalence for 𝐺 𝐿2 /ℚ, with V prim corresponding to the
structure sheaf on the spectral side.

Obstruction Analysis Trace
Obstruction 1 (source separation). Fargues–Scholze arXiv:2102.13459 (local geometrisation via Fargues–
Fontaine curve) and Arinkin–Gaitsgory arXiv:1201.6343 (nilpotent singular support) are disjoint source
lists. The Emerton–Gee stack arXiv:1908.07185 is disjoint from both.

Obstruction 2 (conventions). Singular-support conventions in Arinkin–Gaitsgory follow the de Rham
shift; Fargues–Scholze follows the pro-étale shift on diamonds. The comparison is done via the Bhatt–
Lurie prismatic-Nygaard convention of arXiv:2201.06120, which bridges both. The comparison is medi-
ated by prismatic Nygaard.

Obstruction 3 (ambient categories). LHS is a stable presentable ∞-category of D-modules on an adelic
quotient; RHS is an ∞-category of ind-coherent sheaves with nilpotent singular support on a derived
formal algebraic stack. Via Gaitsgory–Rozenblyum’s AMS DAG monographs the categories sit in the
same ambient (∞, 2)-category of correspondences.

Obstruction 4 (missing hypothesis). The sph-finite cut on the LHS is critical: without it the full auto-
morphic category is too large (contains continuous spectrum and Eisenstein contributions requiring
explicit parametrisation). Fargues–Scholze supply local geometrisation and spectral action; they do not
identify this sph-finite automorphic category with IndCohNilp on the Emerton–Gee stack. Residual:
local categorical comparison.

Obstruction 5 (false functoriality). Functoriality under Hecke operators 𝑇𝑝 at every prime is the key

is required place-by-place and across places (composition of Hecke operators at distinct primes). The
cross-prime compatibility is the global gluing obstruction. Residual: local comparison plus global
gluing.

Remark 21.5.2 (conditional structure of Chapter 21.5.1). Steps 1, 2, 4 of Chapter 21.5.1 draw on Julia–
Spector (primon gas), Bost–Connes (Hecke 𝐶 ∗ -algebra), and Tate (adelic Poisson); these are the classical
inputs. Step 3 is conditional on arithmetic Positselski (Chapter 24.1.5). The 𝜇 = 0-invariant condition
of that conjecture is satisfied for the arithmetic Heisenberg: the cyclotomic 𝜇-invariant of the universal
cyclotomic deformation of the Heisenberg Fock is zero (Ferrero–Washington Ann. Math. 109, 1979 for
the abelian case; conjectural in general, but satisfied for the abelian Heisenberg).
Corollary 21.5.3 (forward implication of P1). (conditional on Chapter 12.5.2). Assuming
𝜅GAr + ( 𝜅 ! )GAr = 0, the functional equation for Λ 𝜁 , and hence for 𝜉ℝ , holds. Arithmetic Positselski
(Chapter 24.1.5) is not required.

Proof. Assume 𝜅GAr + ( 𝜅 ! )GAr = 0. Step 1 (Julia–Spector primon gas) identifies the bar generating func-
tion with 𝜁 ( 𝑠 ). Step 2 (Bost–Connes Koszul duality, Chapter 12.5.2) identifies the bar-cobar pairing
with the adelic Mellin transform computing Λ 𝜁 ( 𝑠 ). Under the hypothesis, the bar-cobar pairing is ℤ/2-
equivariant. Step 4 (Tate 1950) gives the Fourier symmetry F𝔸 Θ = Θ, and change of variables 𝑎 ↦→ 𝑎 −1
completes the derivation of Λ 𝜁 ( 𝑠 ) = Λ 𝜁 (1 − 𝑠 ). The pole-cleared 𝜉ℝ then has the same involution. Step
3 (bar-cobar weight computation) is not invoked; the hypothesis supplies equivariance directly.

21.7    P3: Unitarity of V prim
Statement
P3 asserts that V prim admits a positive-definite Hermitian form compatible with arithmetic Koszul
self-duality.

Obstruction Analysis Trace
Obstructions 1–4. Sources: Weil 1967 (Basic Number Theory), Bost–Connes 1995, Selberg 1956 (Rankin–
Selberg positivity, Tata Institute Bombay 1956). Disjoint.

Obstruction 5 (false functoriality). Positive-definiteness at each place is classical. Across places: the
restricted tensor product preserves positive-definiteness when all factors are unital positive-definite.

Obstruction 6 (unproved equivalence). Compatibility between the Petersson/Tamagawa inner product
and the arithmetic Koszul pairing is a verification: both pair V prim with (V prim ) ! , and the two pairings
agree iff the Koszul pairing is the adelic Fourier pairing. Residual: explicit identification of Koszul
pairing with Petersson pairing.

from the derived-centre structure) with the Petersson pairing (arising from the adelic 𝐿 2 -structure).
Both pair the same two objects; the claim is that they coincide.

        The Riemann Hypothesis Reformulation

        The zero-placement clause of F-RH is the Riemann Hypothesis. The full F-RH assertion also contains
        the structural assertion that V prim carries a positive-definite Hermitian structure compatible with arith-
        metic Koszul self-duality and arithmetic Tate’s functional equation and explicit formula. The structural
        theorems of Chapter 21 place P1, P2, P3 on their stated domains; the zero-placement condition is a
        determinant-divisor and positive-trace assertion, equivalently a positive Hilbert–Pólya Li trace after the
        regularised trace identity has been supplied.

        22.1   The Conjecture F-RH
        Conjecture 22.1.1 (arithmetic unitary zero-placement: F-RH). V prim admits a unique positive-definite
        Hermitian structure compatible with arithmetic Koszul self-duality 𝜅 Ar + ( 𝜅 ! ) Ar = 0 and with Tate’s
        completed-zeta character and explicit formula. Under this structure, the non-trivial zeros of the entire
        character 𝜉ℝ ( 𝑠 ) of V prim lie on the self-dual locus Re( 𝑠 ) = 1/2.
        Remark 22.1.2 (zero-placement and RH). The Tate character supplied by P2 is the meromorphic com-
        pleted zeta function
                                           Λ 𝜁 ( 𝑠 ) := 𝜋 − 𝑠/2 Γ ( 𝑠 /2) 𝜁 ( 𝑠 ) ,
        with simple poles at 𝑠 = 0, 1. The entire Li–Hadamard object is
                                                          1
                                               𝜉ℝ ( 𝑠 ) := 𝑠 ( 𝑠 − 1) Λ 𝜁 ( 𝑠 ) .
                                                          2
        Here 𝜉 means 𝜉ℝ unless Λ 𝜁 is written explicitly. The zeros of 𝜉ℝ are exactly the non-trivial zeros of 𝜁 ;
        the gamma poles cancel the negative even trivial zeros of 𝜁 , and the factor 𝑠 ( 𝑠 − 1) removes the Tate
        poles. Thus the zero-placement assertion in F-RH is exactly RH. The existence and compatibility of the
        positive Hermitian structure are additional arithmetic structure, not a consequence of RH alone.

Remark 22.2.2 (HP–Li as residual condition). With P1, P2, P3 resolved to Theorem or Theorem-
conditional, the zero-placement clause of F-RH reduces to the construction of the Hilbert–Pólya
zero-divisor operator and to HP–Li positivity. This is the arithmetic form of the classical Weil–Li
positivity problem, not a formal consequence of Virasoro representation theory.

non-trivial zeros. Thus H-PAr is a statement about the primary determinant 𝜉ℝ , while the meromorphic
Tate character Λ 𝜁 belongs to the cohomological/superdeterminant surface.

        Proof. HP–Li gives 𝜆𝑛 ≥ 0 for all 𝑛 ≥ 1 by Chapter 22.3.8. Li positivity is equivalent to RH (Li 1997,
        Chapter 22.3.1); this is exactly the zero-placement clause of F-RH (Chapter 22.1.2).

        Remark 22.3.11 (one-directional implication and operator discipline). The polynomial ( 𝐿0Ar ) 𝑛 − ( 𝐿0Ar −
        id) 𝑛 is not Li’s transform; 𝐿0Ar would need to serve simultaneously as Fock energy, Bost–Connes Hamil-
        tonian, and determinant-trace operator, three incompatible roles (see Chapter 22.3.6). The correct state-
        ment is the one-directional HP–Li positivity ⇒ zero-placement, where H-PAr supplies Θ𝜉 . The converse
        is the assertion that zero-placement supplies a positive Weil trace representation of the full zero distribu-
        tion; this is the Hilbert–Pólya/Connes–Deninger positivity problem.
        Remark 22.3.12 (content of F-RH as a reformulation). F-RH separates RH from the extra arithmetic
        structures carried by V prim .
          (i) The spectral object is made precise: the self-adjoint determinant form of H-PAr is a Hilbert–Pólya
              realisation of RH, while HP–Li positivity is Li’s scalar RH-equivalent positivity written through
              the zero-divisor operator after the trace identity is fixed.
22.4. Comparison to Existing RH Mechanisms                                                                  141


  (ii) A structural constraint on zero-placement emerges: the Petersson positivity of P3 propagates
       through the Weil/Connes trace functional to impose positivity of the Li transforms, provided the
       trace representation is determinate.
 (iii) The reformulation connects RH mechanisms (Connes, Deninger, Meyer) to positive-trace and
       factorisation methods, with the arithmetic explicit formula replacing compact-CFT modularity.
 (iv) Admissible approximants to the Li/Weil test functions can be evaluated against the Bost–Connes
       and Hecke trace formulae. Positivity is a distributional trace question, not finite Fock positivity
       of 𝑇𝑛 .

Remark 22.4.1 (relations). (i) HP–Li positivity is Li positivity written on the Hilbert–Pólya zero-
       divisor operator Θ𝜉 . It implies zero-placement, hence RH, via Chapter 22.3.10. A Virasoro poly-
       nomial 𝑇𝑛 is not a substitute for this transform.
  (ii) The zero-placement clause is governed by Weil positivity: Weil’s inner product on test functions
       corresponds to the Petersson inner product on V prim via Tate’s restricted tensor product. F-RH
       adds the arithmetic Hermitian, Koszul, and completed-zeta trace structures around this clause.
 (iii) F-RH embeds Hilbert–Pólya explicitly as H-PAr (Chapter 22.3.2): it asks for a self-adjoint operator
       𝐴, the positive form from P3, the determinant divisor of Θ𝜉 = 1/2 + 𝑖 𝐴, the regularised non-
       trivial-zero trace distribution, and ℤ/2-symmetry under the arithmetic 𝑆 -modular involution
       from P1. F-RH does not replace Hilbert–Pólya: H-PAr is a separate spectral hypothesis in the
       sufficient implication below.
 (iv) F-RH is closer to Connes than to Deninger: both Connes and F-RH use unitarity plus Bost–
       Connes positivity; Deninger postulates a cohomology theory that F-RH does not need. The differ-
       ence from Connes is that F-RH carries the positivity through arithmetic holomorphic-topological
       (HT) observables and a Weil-positive trace rather than through the bare trace-formula construc-
       tion.

22.7    Relation to the Arithmetic Branch Essential Theorem
The arithmetic branch’s essential theorem (Chapter 19.2.1, Chapter 21.5.1) is

                               𝜅GAr + ( 𝜅 ! )GAr = 0 ⇐⇒ 𝜉 ( 𝑠 ) = 𝜉 (1 − 𝑠 ) .

This gives the functional equation (geometric self-duality of 𝜉ℝ ), not RH (spectral zero-placement). RH
is strictly beyond the essential theorem, requiring the additional positive Hilbert–Pólya trace input.
     F-RH asks whether Koszul self-duality, which gives the functional equation, combined with the
positivity of P3 and the explicit-formula content of P2, suffices to deliver the spectral zero-placement
that RH asserts. The implication in the chiral-algebra formalism is conditional on H-PAr and HP–Li
positivity. Those two statements are the Hilbert–Pólya form of RH native to this formalism.

22.8    The F-RH Reduction
   (i) The zero-placement clause of F-RH (Chapter 22.1.1) is exactly RH (Chapter 22.1.2). F-RH also
       asks for the positive Hermitian structure compatible with arithmetic Koszul self-duality, Tate’s
       functional equation, and the explicit formula.
  (ii) The zero-placement clause is implied by H-PAr and HP–Li positivity together with P1 + P2 + P3
       (Chapter 22.2.1).
 (iii) The zero-placement clause is implied by HP–Li positivity (positive Hilbert–Pólya trace; Chap-
       ter 22.3.10) via Li’s criterion, given the determinant and trace identities of H-PAr . If the full
       determinant-trace H-PAr hypothesis is assumed, zero-placement is already part of the determinant-
       trace realisation. The converse direction from zero-placement to HP–Li is the positive-trace reali-
       sation problem.
 (iv) Li’s coefficients 𝜆𝑛 are Hilbert–Pólya transform traces of Θ𝜉 (Chapter 22.3.8).
  (v) Li positivity and Weil positivity govern the zero-placement clause. F-RH joins this clause to the
       arithmetic Hermitian, Koszul, and completed-zeta trace structures.
 (vi) The sufficient implication to RH uses four inputs: arith. Positselski, Koszul–Pet compat, H-
       PAr , and HP–Li positivity (Chapter 22.6.1). This is the four-input conditional conjunction stated
       in Chapter 39 and made precise as Chapter 39.3.1: each input carries its own analytic content
       (five Positselski sub-items, KMS1 /GNS identification beyond the sph-fin cuspidal core, zeta-zero
144                                    Chapter 22. The Riemann Hypothesis Reformulation


      determinant-trace matching, RH-equivalent positive trace), and the conjunction implies zero-
      placement.
(vii) RH is strictly beyond the branch’s essential theorem (functional equation), and HP–Li positivity
      is the Li positive-trace form of RH within the chiral-algebra formalism. The operator dictionary
      of Chapter 22.3.11 preserves only the forward implication HP–Li⇒zero-placement; the converse
      is the positive determinant-trace realisation problem (Chapter 36.4.16) and does not help the
      forward direction.

Arithmetic Virasoro Positivity Bootstrap

With the determinant form of Chapter 22 in place, the Virasoro-polynomial sequence 𝑇𝑛Vir = ( 𝐿0Vir ) 𝑛 −
( 𝐿0Vir − id) 𝑛 is not the Li operator. It proves ﬁnite-sector Fock positivity, but it does not construct a Hilbert–
Pólya operator and it does not give RH. The RH-strength input is the positive Hilbert–Pólya trace of
L𝑛 = id − (id − Θ𝜉−1 ) 𝑛 from Chapter 22.

Here 𝐿0Vir is the Fock/Virasoro conformal-energy operator. It is not the Hilbert–Pólya determinant-trace

Thus 𝑇𝑛Vir is a legitimate Fock polynomial on any common Virasoro spectral core, but it is not Li’s

Remark 23.1.2 (why 𝑇𝑛Vir is not the Li object). Two conventions for Li’s criterion circulate in the literature.
The original Li 1997 J. Number Theory paper defines 𝜆𝑛 = 𝜌 (1 − (1 − 1/ 𝜌) 𝑛 ); Bombieri–Lagarias J.

Consequently, every claim below involving 𝑇𝑛Vir is a formal Fock/Virasoro claim unless it is explicitly
restated in terms of L𝑛 and the positive Weil–Connes trace.

Conditional Chain: VB∗ ⇒ Li Positivity ⇔ RH
Proposition 23.1.3 (formal Virasoro positivity is not Li positivity). . Positivity of the formal
Virasoro polynomial 𝑇𝑛Vir on finite Fock sectors does not imply 𝜆𝑛 ≥ 0, and therefore does not imply
RH. The one-directional RH implication in Vol IV is instead

                                      HP–Li =⇒ 𝜆𝑛 ≥ 0 ∀𝑛 ⇐⇒ RH,

where HP–Li is the positive trace statement of Chapter 22.3.10.

Proof. Li’s criterion is Li 1997 J. Number Theory, reproduced in Bombieri–Lagarias J. Number Theory
77 (1999). The Li summand is 1 − (1 − 1/ 𝜌) 𝑛 . The spectral transform realising this summand is therefore

𝑧 ↦→ 1 − (1 − 𝑧 −1 ) 𝑛 applied to the zero operator 𝑧 = Θ𝜉 . The polynomial 𝑥 𝑛 − ( 𝑥 − 1) 𝑛 applied to
a Virasoro energy 𝑥 = 𝐿0Vir is a different function of a different operator. Positivity of the latter is a
Fock calculation; it has no trace identity with Li’s coefficients unless the Hilbert–Pólya trace identity has
already been replaced by the correct Θ𝜉 -transform. The HP–Li implication follows from Chapter 22.3.10.


Remark 23.1.4 (what is genuinely equivalent). The known RH-equivalent positivity languages are Li
positivity, Weil positivity for the number-field explicit formula, and the positive zero-measure conjecture
for Θ𝜉 , VB∗core . Under explicit hypotheses these languages give the same positivity condition. None of
the RH-equivalent positivity statements is unconditional here.
Remark 23.1.5 (the level at which RH lives). RH lives on the zero-divisor operator Θ𝜉 = 1/2 + 𝑖 𝐻HP , not
on the Virasoro energy operator. The Bost–Connes Hamiltonian and the Virasoro 𝐿0 give Euler weights
and Fock energies; neither carries div 𝜉ℝ . A real spectral measure appears only after H-PAr supplies 𝐻HP
and identifies det∞ ( 𝑠 − Θ𝜉 ) with 𝜉ℝ ( 𝑠 ). VB∗ , in its RH-strength form, is therefore a positivity statement
for the Weil–Connes trace of functions of Θ𝜉 , together with determinacy of the corresponding zero
measure.

23.2    Obstructions
Virasoro levels
For 𝑛 = 1 one has 𝑇1Vir = id. For 𝑛 = 2 one has

                                    ( 𝐿0Vir ) 2 − ( 𝐿0Vir − id) 2 = 2 𝐿0Vir − id.

Thus 𝑇2Vir ⪰ 0 is the Fock threshold 𝐿0Vir ⪰ 21 id. It is not a statement about zeta zeros. Li’s coefficient
at level 2 is the trace of 𝑧 ↦→ 1 − (1 − 𝑧 −1 ) 2 on Θ𝜉 , and equality between these two functional calculi
would itself be an additional Hilbert–Pólya theorem.

Moment problem
The Hamburger moment problem belongs to the regularised spectral measure of Θ𝜉 . There is no identity

                                              Trreg (𝑇𝑛Vir ) = 𝑛𝜆𝑛 .

The valid moment sequence is obtained from the zero-divisor operator and the Weil–Connes trace.
Stieltjes’ theorem supplies the algebraic test: a sequence is the moment sequence of a positive measure
on [0, ∞) precisely when all Hankel and shifted Hankel minors are non-negative.

Kac determinant
At 𝑐 = 2, the Kac parametrisation gives

                                           6
                                 1−              = 2,          𝑚 ( 𝑚 + 1) = −6.
                                      𝑚 ( 𝑚 + 1)
The null weights form the countable set { ℎ𝑟,𝑠 (2) : 𝑟, 𝑠 ≥ 1}. Outside this set the contravariant form is
non-degenerate. Non-degeneracy is weaker than positivity; the Petersson sign is not determined by the
non-vanishing of the Kac determinant.

Weil trace
Weil positivity is a positivity theorem for the explicit formula and is equivalent to RH over number fields.
In the Vol IV notation its operator representative is the positive regularised trace of L𝑛 ( Θ𝜉 ), not a trace
of 𝑇𝑛Vir . Koszul–Petersson compatibility can identify the Weil trace pairing with a Petersson pairing on
admissible arithmetic states; it cannot identify the Virasoro energy spectrum with the zero divisor.

de Branges datum
For a Hermite–Biehler function 𝐸 , the de Branges kernel is

                                               𝐸 (𝑤 ) 𝐸 ( 𝑧 ) − 𝐸 ∗ (𝑤 ) 𝐸 ∗ ( 𝑧 )

The real entire function Ξ ( 𝑧 ) = 𝜉ℝ (1/2 + 𝑖 𝑧 ) satisfies Ξ∗ = Ξ, so Ξ itself is not a Hermite–Biehler
function. A de Branges reformulation of RH requires a genuine datum 𝐸 whose divisor controls the
divisor of Ξ. The Hermite–Biehler condition is then part of the RH-strength input, not a consequence
of formal Virasoro positivity.

Corollary 23.3.4 ( 𝑛 = 2 is not a zero-placement theorem). . The implication

                       𝑇2Vir ⪰ 0     =⇒      Re( 𝜌) = 1/2 for every non-trivial zero 𝜌

is false without an additional Hilbert–Pólya identification of the Virasoro energy with the zero-divisor

Proof. The spectrum of 𝐿0Vir is the conformal-energy spectral measure of the Fock representation. The

Remark 23.3.5 (the spectral barrier). The 𝑛 = 2 Virasoro calculation is a threshold calculation inside
the Fock representation. The RH barrier is the construction of the zero-divisor operator Θ𝜉 and of
a positive trace on its Li transforms. Confusing these two operators turns Fock positivity into a false
Hilbert–Pólya argument.

Corollary 23.3.7 (finite Li data are scalar data). . For any finite set 𝐹 ⊂ ℕ, the inequalities
𝜆𝑛 ≥ 0 for 𝑛 ∈ 𝐹 are scalar inequalities for the Li transforms L𝑛 = 1 − (1 − Θ𝜉−1 ) 𝑛 . They do not imply
operator positivity of 𝑇𝑛Vir , and they do not imply RH. Bombieri–Lagarias bounds and finite numerical
evaluations are therefore finite scalar controls, not Virasoro positivity theorems.

Proof. Li’s criterion requires 𝜆𝑛 ≥ 0 for every 𝑛 ≥ 1. A finite set of inequalities is therefore not equivalent
to RH. The identity 𝜆𝑛 = Trreg (L𝑛 ) is a scalar trace identity for Θ𝜉 . A positive trace of one operator
does not force positivity of another operator: a diagonal matrix with eigenvalues −1 and 2 has positive
trace and is not positive. The Virasoro polynomial 𝑇𝑛Vir is a different functional calculus from L𝑛 .

Remark 23.3.8 (the trace-positivity gap). The number-theoretic trace is attached to L𝑛 ( Θ𝜉 ), not to 𝑇𝑛Vir .
Li positivity for all 𝑛 is equivalent to RH. Operator positivity of a Virasoro polynomial is a separate
Fock statement, and a scalar trace cannot bridge the two without a positive, determinate Weil–Connes
representation of the zero measure.

Proposition 23.4.3 (the defect measure is not a Li–Stieltjes moment model). . The off-line

Hamburger Moment Determinacy
Theorem 23.4.4 (Hamburger reformulation for the formal 𝑇𝑛 ). . The following equivalence is a

   (i) Formal positivity: 𝑇𝑛Vir ⪰ 0 for all 𝑛 ≥ 1 on a fixed self-adjoint spectral model.
  (ii) The associated spectral measure is a positive measure supported on [1/2, ∞).
 (iii) For the shifted moments 𝜈𝑘 := [1/2,∞) ( 𝑥 − 1/2) 𝑘 𝑑𝜇 ( 𝑥 ), all Hankel minors 𝐻𝑛 :=

      every 𝑛 ≥ 0.
This theorem is not an independent proof of RH and does not connect 𝑇𝑛Vir to Li’s coefficients.

                                    𝑇2Vir ( 𝑥 ) = 𝑥 2 − ( 𝑥 − 1) 2 = 2 𝑥 − 1,

Remark 23.4.5 (moment information). Chapter 23.4.4 records the formal moment-determinacy appara-
tus that would become relevant after a true Hilbert–Pólya spectral measure is constructed. In particular:
• Testing a genuine positive spectral measure level-by-level becomes testing Hankel determinants 𝐻𝑛
  level-by-level, a finite numerical procedure at each 𝑛.
150                                        Chapter 23. Arithmetic Virasoro Positivity Bootstrap


• Known numerical bounds for Li coefficients do not test these Hankel determinants; they test a different
  holomorphic transform of the zero divisor.
• Known structural estimates on Li coefficients and Voros regularised sums do not supply lower bounds
  for the shifted Stieltjes minors above.
• The gap between known and needed becomes precisely specified: unconditional lower bounds on
  𝐻𝑛(1) for all 𝑛.
The equivalent Hilbert–Pólya condition is the construction of the positive zero measure itself.

Unitarity Gap at Special Weights
Remark 23.5.4 (the gap between non-degeneracy and positivity). Chapter 23.5.3 establishes non-degeneracy,
not positivity. Two Hermitian forms can be non-degenerate (no null vectors) without being positive-
definite (a form of signature (+, −, +, −, . . .) is non-degenerate). The Friedan–Qiu–Shenker 1986 𝑐 < 1
analysis converts non-degeneracy to positivity via the Kac determinant sign pattern: when 𝑐 < 1 is not
23.6. Fock-Combinatorial Identity                                                                               151


in the discrete unitary series, the sign of det𝑛𝑐,ℎ oscillates, producing at least one negative eigenvalue and
refuting unitarity. The 𝑐 = 2 case is outside the discrete 𝑐 < 1 minimal unitary series, but it lies in the
standard 𝑐 ≥ 1 free-boson unitary regime. Hence the FQS sign-oscillation argument for non-minimal
𝑐 < 1 modules does not apply.

       23.7    Reduction to the Irreducible Core Obstruction
       The Core Statement
       Theorem 23.7.1 (conditional reduction to the zero-operator core). (conditional on P2, P3, H-PAr , the
       primary tensor decomposition, and a positive regularised trace). Under these hypotheses, the RH-strength
       positivity statement reduces to the following zero-operator statement:
(VB∗core ) Zero-operator spectral positivity. The operator Θ𝜉 = 1/2 + 𝑖 𝐻HP satisfies det∞ ( 𝑠 − Θ𝜉 ) = 𝜉ℝ ( 𝑠 ), and
           the regularised Weil–Connes trace on the Li transforms L𝑛 ( Θ𝜉 ) is positive for every 𝑛 ≥ 1.
       The Bost–Connes zero-mode lattice supplies the Euler/KMS regularisation of the trace. It is not the
       spectrum of Θ𝜉 .

       Proof. H-PAr gives the determinant identity for Θ𝜉 . By Chapter 22.3.8, the Li coefficient 𝜆𝑛 is the
       regularised trace of L𝑛 ( Θ𝜉 ). Positivity of these traces for every 𝑛 is Li positivity, hence RH by Li’s
       theorem. Conversely, RH is the support condition for the spectral measure of Θ𝜉 . The Bost–Connes
       spectrum {log 𝑚 } enters only through the regularisation giving the Euler product; no step identifies it
       with the determinant divisor of Θ𝜉 .
23.8. Comparison to Classical RH Equivalents                                                                    153


The Named Obstruction
Corollary 23.7.2 (the irreducible core of VB ∗ ). (conditional on the hypotheses of Chapter 23.7.1).
The irreducible core is the positive zero-divisor measure problem for Θ𝜉 . Replacing Θ𝜉 by the Bost–
Connes Hamiltonian 𝑁BC replaces the zero divisor by the Euler eigenvalues and therefore destroys the
Hilbert–Pólya statement.
Remark 23.7.3 (core equivalence). (VB∗core ) is not a weaker statement than VB∗ under the Hilbert–Pólya
and positive-trace hypotheses; it is the zero-operator form of the same condition.
   (i) The zero divisor is carried by Θ𝜉 .
  (ii) The Euler product is carried by the Bost–Connes KMS trace.
 (iii) The equality between the two is the Hilbert–Pólya trace bridge.
 (iv) The Bost–Connes phase transition at 𝛽 = 1 records the pole of 𝜁 ; it is not a statement about phase
       transitions on the critical line.

23.9    Zero-Divisor Condition
The Precise Condition
The RH-strength positivity statement is equivalent to the following condition:
Deﬁnition 23.9.1 (the Vol IV zero-divisor condition). . The Vol IV zero-divisor condition is the following
statement:
       There is a normal zero-divisor operator Θ𝜉 = 1/2 + 𝑖 𝐻HP whose determinant divisor
       is div 𝜉ℝ , and whose Weil–Connes trace is supported on 1/2 + 𝑖 ℝ. The Bost–Connes              (R IV )
       zero-mode gives the Euler/KMS regularisation of the trace; it does not carry div 𝜉ℝ .

Theorem 23.9.2 (R IV implies the Riemann Hypothesis). . R IV ⇒ RH. Conversely, RH gives only
the zero-placement part of R IV ; it does not construct the normal zero-divisor operator, the determinant
divisor, the Weil–Connes trace, or the Bost–Connes regularisation.

Proof. By definition, R IV includes a Θ𝜉 -determinant divisor and Weil–Connes trace concentrated on
the critical line. Since det∞ ( 𝑠 − Θ𝜉 ) = 𝜉ℝ ( 𝑠 ), this is exactly the zero-placement assertion for the non-
trivial zeros of 𝜁 , hence RH by Chapter 22.1.2. The converse would require the extra operator-realization
data named in the statement; zero placement alone does not supply it.

Virasoro Boundary
Remark 23.9.3 (structural change). The arithmetic Virasoro reduction gives:
   (i) Closed 𝑛 = 1 unconditionally (Chapter 23.3.1).
  (ii) Reduced 𝑛 = 2 to the formal Virasoro threshold 𝐿0Vir ⪰ (1/2)id, not to zero placement
       (Chapter 23.3.4).
 (iii) Established Fock-level positivity for the archimedean sector at every 𝑛 (Chapter 23.6.4).
 (iv) Reformulated the zero-measure problem as a Hamburger moment determinacy problem for Θ𝜉
       (Chapter 23.4.4).
  (v) Proved the Kac determinant at 𝑐 = 2 is non-zero at generic weights (Chapter 23.5.2), establishing
       absence of null-vector unitarity obstruction.
 (vi) Placed HP–Li in correspondence with Weil positivity (Chapter 23.8.2) and the de Branges Hermite-
       Biehler framework.
(vii) The RH-strength condition is a single zero-measure positivity statement for Θ𝜉 (VB∗core , Chap-
       ter 23.7.1).
VB∗ itself remains open, as it is equivalent to RH.
Remark 23.9.4 (VB∗core boundary). The assertion (VB∗core ) contains the following independent analytic
inputs:
   (i) A second KMS-positivity input beyond Bost–Connes: a constraint on the zero-divisor measure
       forcing critical-line concentration.
  (ii) An arithmetic-modular bootstrap input: a Kac-formula-style analysis of the arithmetic Virasoro
       algebra on the Bost–Connes 𝐶 ∗ -algebra, extracting unitarity from null-vector absence.
 (iii) An 𝑛 → ∞ asymptotic input: a moment-generating-function bootstrap strong enough to close
       the 𝑛 → ∞ limit of 𝜆𝑛 scaling.
23.10. Arithmetic Zhu Finiteness Test                                                                      155


The first input belongs to the arithmetic site of Connes–Consani arXiv:1405.4527. The second is the
𝐶 ∗ -algebraic analogue of Friedan–Qiu–Shenker. The third is an asymptotic moment problem.

23.10     Arithmetic Zhu Finiteness Test
The tempting shortcut is Verlinde finite-dimensionality: prove that the primary Bost–Connes core is an
arithmetic Zhu-finite object, obtain a finite-dimensional Hermitian modular functor, and read positivity
from ordinary linear algebra. The shortcut fails on the full zeta object.
Deﬁnition 23.10.1 (Euler-faithful arithmetic Zhu quotient). . An Euler-faithful arithmetic Zhu quotient
of the primary Bost–Connes core is a quotient 𝑄 of the zero-mode lattice 𝐿 = ℓ 2 (ℕ× ) satisfying:
  (i) the Bost–Connes operators descend:

        where 𝛿 𝑚 is the image of 𝛿𝑚 ∈ 𝐿 ;
  (ii) the KMS Hamiltonian 𝐻 = log 𝑁 descends with 𝐻 𝛿 𝑚 = (log 𝑚) 𝛿 𝑚 whenever 𝛿 𝑚 ≠ 0;
 (iii) the ordinary KMS character of the quotient is the full Bost–Connes Euler product:

Theorem 23.10.2 (no Euler-faithful Zhu finiteness). . No Euler-faithful arithmetic Zhu quotient
of the primary Bost–Connes core is Zhu finite.

Proof. If 𝑄 were finite-dimensional, the trace Tr𝑄 ( 𝑒 − 𝛽𝐻 ) would be a finite sum 𝑗𝑟 =1 𝑎𝑗 𝑒 − 𝛽𝐸𝑗 after
                                                                                          P
diagonalising the finite-dimensional self-adjoint operator 𝐻 . In particular it extends to an entire function
of 𝛽 . Euler-faithfulness requires this finite sum to equal 𝜁 ( 𝛽 ) on the half-plane Re 𝛽 > 1. By the identity
theorem the meromorphic continuation of 𝜁 would be entire, contradicting its simple pole at 𝛽 = 1.
Hence 𝑄 is infinite-dimensional.
    Equivalently, the faithful Bost–Connes action of Chapter 7.3.2 sends 𝛿1 to 𝛿𝑚 by 𝜇𝑚 𝛿1 = 𝛿𝑚 . Keeping
the full Euler product keeps one independent KMS eigenline at every 𝑚 ∈ ℕ× . A finite Zhu quotient
must kill or identify infinitely many of these lines, and then it no longer has character 𝜁 ( 𝛽 ).

Corollary 23.10.3 (Verlinde finite-dimensionality cannot close full RH). . Arithmetic
Zhu/Verlinde finite-dimensionality cannot prove VB∗core for the full V prim while preserving the
completed zeta partition function. The only Zhu-finite quotients compatible with the Bost–Connes
action are finite-prime or finite-conductor truncations; their characters are finite Euler products or
finite Dirichlet polynomials, not 𝜉 ( 𝑠 ).

Proof. By Chapter 23.10.2, a finite-dimensional quotient cannot be Euler-faithful. A quotient supported
on a finite set 𝑆 of primes has character 𝑝 ∈ 𝑆 (1 − 𝑝 − 𝛽 ) −1 , possibly with an archimedean Tate factor.
                                          Q
Such a finite Euler product is a finite-level arithmetic modular-functor object; it is not the zeta ob-
ject whose zero-placement is RH. Therefore finite-dimensional Hermitian linear algebra can test finite
windows, but it cannot supply the missing positivity for the full Θ𝜉 -spectral measure.
156                                   Chapter 23. Arithmetic Virasoro Positivity Bootstrap


Remark 23.10.4 (central charge does not rescue Zhu ﬁniteness). The residue value 𝑟 𝜁 = 2 of Chapter 14.4.1
is a determinant-rank scalar, not a finite rank and not a trace. Chapter 14 proves that the full infinite
tensor has no global Virasoro action. Thus 𝑟 𝜁 = 2 cannot be used as a 𝐶2 -cofiniteness or Zhu-finiteness
input.
Remark 23.10.5 (surviving direction). The finite-dimensional construction survives only as a finite-
window technology: truncate to finitely many primes or to bounded conductor, prove the corresponding
arithmetic modular functor is finite, compute its Hermitian form, and compare its limiting trace to
the Bost–Connes KMS trace. Any limiting theorem strong enough to recover VB∗core must add a new
positivity or compactness input beyond Zhu finite-dimensionality at finite level.

23.11   Zero-Measure Conjecture
Conjecture 23.11.1 (VB∗core : the Vol IV form of RH). . The zero-divisor operator Θ𝜉 = 1/2 + 𝑖 𝐻HP , with
div det∞ ( 𝑠 − Θ𝜉 ) = div 𝜉ℝ , has determinant divisor and Weil–Connes trace supported on 1/2 + 𝑖 ℝ.
Equivalently, all non-trivial zeros of 𝜁 lie on the critical line.
Remark 23.11.2 (the conjecture is RH). Chapter 23.11.1 is, verbatim, the Riemann Hypothesis. The arith-
metic chiral-algebra formulation asks for a positive, determinate Weil–Connes trace and determinant
divisor on the zero-divisor operator Θ𝜉 . The Bost–Connes algebra supplies the Euler regularisation and
KMS weight, in the sense of Connes’ adelic trace formula; it does not supply the determinant divisor by
itself.
Remark 23.11.3 (size of VB∗core ). Any unconditional proof of Chapter 23.11.1 would be an unconditional
proof of RH, a Millennium Prize problem. No finite estimate is meaningful. Partial reductions have the
following mathematical sizes:
Bombieri-Lagarias-style sharpening at specific 𝑛. substantial local theorem.
Kac-determinant analysis at 𝑐 = 2 to low level. finite-level determinant computation.
Moment-problem Hankel analysis. unbounded Hamburger determinacy and lower bounds on all
shifted Hankel minors.
Arithmetic-site incorporation. Connes–Consani arithmetic-site positivity; no unconditional proof
of RH follows.

Arithmetic Positselski Equivalence

This chapter lifts Positselski’s classical comodule–contramodule correspondence (Mem. AMS 996,
arXiv:0905.2621) from ﬁeld coeﬃcients to the Iwasawa algebra Λ = ℤ 𝑝 [[ Γ]]. The Iwasawa 𝜇-invariant is
the precise obstruction: when 𝜇 = 0, the classical correspondence lifts to a Λ-linear equivalence between
co-derived Λ-comodules and contra-derived Λ-contramodules. Applied to the arithmetic Heisenberg
bar coalgebra, this closes the level–weight computation of Step 3 in the proof of P1 (Chapter 21.5.1)
and, conditional on the ﬁve open Positselski sub-items of Chapter 24.1.6, gives the full biconditional
𝜅GAr + ( 𝜅 ! )GAr = 0 ⇔ 𝜉 ( 𝑠 ) = 𝜉 (1 − 𝑠 ).

24.1   Statement and Motivation
Review: Classical Positselski
Let 𝑘 be a field and 𝐶 a conilpotent dg coalgebra over 𝑘 . Positselski (arXiv:0905.2621, Thm. 6.5;
Mem. AMS 996, Ch. 0) constructs two derived categories distinct from the ordinary one:
   (i) The co-derived category Dco ( 𝐶 −comod𝑘 ): the homotopy category of injective complexes of 𝐶 -
       comodules, equivalently the Verdier quotient of the homotopy category by acyclic complexes of
       injectives (Positselski §3.5).
  (ii) The contra-derived category Dctr ( 𝐶 ∨ −contramod𝑘 ): the homotopy category of projective com-
       plexes of contramodules over the dual algebra 𝐶 ∨ , equivalently the Verdier quotient by acyclic
       complexes of projectives (Positselski §3.7).
Theorem 24.1.1 (Positselski 2011, arXiv:0905.2621 Thm. 5.2). . There is a canonical equivalence of
triangulated categories

                                Dco ( 𝐶 −comod𝑘 ) ≃ Dctr ( 𝐶 ∨ −contramod𝑘 ) ,

given on objects by 𝑀 ↦→ Hom𝐶 ( 𝐶, 𝑀 ) = 𝑀 ∨ with the induced contramodule structure.
    The equivalence is the categorical shadow of two-sided Koszul duality: the bar complex of 𝐶 ∨ is
𝐶 , the cobar complex of 𝐶 is 𝐶 ∨ , and the two categories of derived modules (covariant = comodule,
contravariant = contramodule) are swapped by the bar–cobar adjunction.

The Λ-Coeﬃcient Target
Replace the field 𝑘 by the Iwasawa algebra Λ = ℤ 𝑝 [[ Γ]] with Γ = Gal(ℚ( 𝜇 𝑝∞ )/ℚ)  ℤ 𝑝 . The base
Λ is a Noetherian local complete two-dimensional regular ring with maximal ideal 𝔪 = ( 𝑝, 𝛾 − 1) and
residue field 𝔽 𝑝 (Serre 1963, Iwasawa 1973). Its key structural feature is the Λ-module structure theorem:
every finitely generated Λ-module 𝑀 admits a pseudo-isomorphism

Thm. 13.12; Coates–Sujatha 2006 Ch. 2). The Iwasawa 𝜇-invariant is 𝜇 ( 𝑀 ) = 𝑖 𝑎𝑖 ; the 𝜆-invariant is

Remark 24.1.4 (why 𝜇 = 0). The Positselski correspondence relies on injective resolutions of comodules
being compatible with projective resolutions of contramodules. Over a field, this reduces to linear algebra.
Over Λ, the Λ-module structure theorem (Chapter 24.1) introduces two obstructions: the 𝜇-part ( 𝑝-
torsion) and the 𝜆-part (characteristic-polynomial torsion). The 𝜆-part is handled by Iwasawa polynomial
machinery (Coleman–Perrin-Riou, Coates–Sujatha 2006 Ch. 3); the 𝜇-part is the genuine obstruction
to descent (Ferrero–Washington 1979). When 𝜇 = 0, base change along Λ → Λ/ 𝑝Λ = 𝔽 𝑝 [[𝑇 ]]
commutes with the derived operations on both sides, and the classical Positselski equivalence lifts.
Theorem 24.1.5 (main theorem: arithmetic Positselski). (conditional on the ﬁve open sub-items of
Chapter 24.1.6: completed continuous duals; derived completion; faithful lifting; primitive zeta-character
theorem; Koszul-dual Bost–Connes). Let 𝐶 be an arithmetic dg Λ-coalgebra (Chapter 24.1.2) with 𝜇 ( 𝐶 ) =
0 (Chapter 24.1.3). Then there is a canonical equivalence of triangulated categories

lifting the classical Positselski equivalence (Chapter 24.1.1) along the base change Λ → ℚ 𝑝 (reduction
modulo pseudo-null). The lift is compatible with the bar–cobar adjunction ΩΛ ⊣ 𝐵 Λ , and the unit
𝐶 → ΩΛ 𝐵 Λ ( 𝐶 ) and counit 𝐵 Λ ΩΛ ( 𝐴) → 𝐴 are quasi-isomorphisms of Λ-dg-coalgebras and Λ-dg-
algebras respectively, provided 𝜇 ( 𝐶 ) = 0 on the comodule side and the dual 𝜇-invariant (Selmer 𝜇)
vanishes on the contramodule side.

Six independent obstruction constructions test the theorem; each names the obstruction exposed and

Obstruction 1: Base-Change Lift
Obstruction. Does Positselski 2011 arXiv:0905.2621 Thm. 5.2 lift directly along the inclusion of base
rings 𝑘 ↩→ Λ, or along reductions Λ → Λ/ 𝑝Λ = 𝔽 𝑝 [[𝑇 ]] and Λ → Λ/( 𝛾 − 1) = ℤ 𝑝 ?

Attempt 1. Direct base change 𝑘 → Λ fails: Positselski’s proof uses that injective = flat = projective for
𝑘 -modules, which breaks already over ℤ 𝑝 (injective ℤ 𝑝 -modules are ℚ 𝑝 /ℤ 𝑝 -like, not free).

Correction. Replace direct base change by a two-step lift. First reduce Λ → Λ/ 𝑝Λ = 𝔽 𝑝 [[𝑇 ]], a
discrete valuation ring with uniformizer 𝑇 . Over 𝔽 𝑝 [[𝑇 ]], Positselski’s 2018 contraherent-cosheaf ma-
chinery (arXiv:1209.2995 Thm. 4.6.5) extends the correspondence: the key input is that 𝔽 𝑝 [[𝑇 ]] is a
Noetherian local regular one-dimensional ring, for which finitely generated flat = projective and the
structure theorem 𝑀 ∼ (𝔽 𝑝 [[𝑇 ]]) 𝑟 ⊕ 𝔽 𝑝 [[𝑇 ]]/𝑇 𝑎𝑖 gives a controllable injective resolution tower.
                                        L
Second, lift along Λ → 𝔽 𝑝 [[𝑇 ]] via Nakayama’s lemma plus the completeness of Λ with respect to
𝔪 = ( 𝑝, 𝛾 − 1).

Conclusion. Base change works in two steps: Λ → 𝔽 𝑝 [[𝑇 ]] is Positselski 2018; the lift from 𝔽 𝑝 [[𝑇 ]]
to Λ uses Nakayama plus complete Noetherianity. The 𝜇 = 0 hypothesis is the precise condition that
162                                            Chapter 24. Arithmetic Positselski Equivalence


the two-step lift preserves the bar–cobar structure: without 𝜇 = 0, there is a 𝑝-torsion kernel 𝑝 𝑁 𝐶
obstructing descent to 𝔽 𝑝 [[𝑇 ]]. With 𝜇 = 0 as the explicit hypothesis.

Obstruction 2: Co-Derived vs Contra-Derived Over Λ
Obstruction. Is there a Λ-coefficient analogue of the classical co-derived / contra-derived distinction,
and does it coincide with the derived-category framework used in Iwasawa theory?

Attempt 1. A naive Λ-co-derived category might be the Verdier quotient of 𝐾 ( 𝐶 −comodΛ ) by com-
plexes of acyclic injectives, where injective = injective over Λ. This fails: over Λ, injective hulls involve
the Pontryagin dual Λ∨ = Homcts ( Λ, ℚ 𝑝 /ℤ 𝑝 ) which is not finitely generated (Brumer 1966; Coates–
Sujatha 2006 §1.7), so injective resolutions of comodules explode in size.

Correction. Use the Selmer-complex formalism of Nekovář 2006 (Astérisque 310, Ch. 1–2): Λ-co-
derived categories are the compact-object categories in the homotopy category of complexes of Λ-
comodules whose injective resolutions are admissible in Nekovář’s sense (bounded-below, truncated pro-
étale-finite). Admissibility precisely encodes the Pontryagin-dual finiteness needed to keep the Verdier
quotient tractable. Similarly, the Λ-contra-derived category is the compact objects in the homotopy
category of 𝐶 ∨ -contramodules whose projective resolutions are Greenberg-admissible (Greenberg 2001,
§3).

Conclusion. The Λ-coefficient co-derived and contra-derived categories exist, via Nekovář’s Selmer-
complex formalism. The admissibility conditions translate to 𝜇 ( 𝐶 ) = 0 on the comodule side and
dual Selmer- 𝜇 = 0 on the contramodule side; these are two different statements, but both reduce to
𝜇-invariant vanishing. with the Selmer-complex framework supplying the triangulated structure.

place 𝑝 (as in the main theorem) plus Gaussian Positselski at ∞ (archimedean Fourier self-duality). The
restricted tensor product of local pairings over ℚ with spherical vectors at almost all places (Tate 1950
§2.3; Weil 1967 Ch. VII §1) gives the adelic Positselski pairing.

Conclusion. The archimedean factor is Gaussian Positselski via Fourier self-duality. The Λ-coefficient
Positselski (Chapter 24.1.5) handles finite places; the adelic assembly uses Tate’s restricted tensor product.
The archimedean assertion reduces to Fourier self-duality.

Obstruction 6: Non-Commutative Iwasawa for Non-Abelian 𝐺 𝐿2
Obstruction. Iwasawa theory for 𝐺 𝐿2 is non-commutative: the 𝐺 𝐿2 Iwasawa algebra is
Λ𝐺 𝐿2 = ℤ 𝑝 [[ 𝐺 𝐿2 (ℤ 𝑝 )]], not abelian. Does the Λ-coefficient Positselski correspondence ex-
tend to Λ𝐺 𝐿2 ?

Attempt 1. Lift the commutative proof directly. This fails: the structure theorem Chapter 24.1 is com-
mutative; the non-commutative analogue (Fukaya–Kato 2006 Proc. St. Petersburg Math. Soc. 12, §1–2)
is more restrictive and holds only modulo pseudo-nullity.

Correction. The main application in this chapter is to the G-row claim for the abelian Heisenberg
                                                                                       prim
sub-algebra of the full Iwahori Hecke category. The abelian Heisenberg is precisely VHeis as defined in
Chapter 12 (before non-abelian Iwahori enhancement). For this abelian sub-algebra, Λ reduces to the
commutative cyclotomic Iwasawa algebra, and the main theorem applies directly.
   For the full non-abelian Iwahori-level 𝐺 𝐿2 Hecke category, the correspondence requires the non-
commutative Iwasawa framework (Fukaya–Kato 2006; Coates–Fukaya–Kato–Sujatha–Venjakob 2005
Publ. IHES). The extension is a separate conjecture, not achieved in this chapter. The G-row claim of P1
only needs the abelian sub-algebra case.

Conclusion. For abelian Heisenberg (P1 G-row application), holds. For non-abelian Iwahori level, resid-
ual: non-commutative arithmetic Positselski (Chapter 24.7).

24.3    Iwasawa Preliminaries
The proof of Chapter 24.1.5 requires three structural facts about finitely generated Λ-modules: the
structure theorem and its 𝜇-invariant criterion, the bounds on injective and projective resolution length,
and the coherence of these resolutions under base change when 𝜇 = 0.

Λ-Modules and Structure Theorem
Proposition 24.3.1 ( Λ -module structure theorem). . Let Λ = ℤ 𝑝 [[ Γ]] and let 𝑀 be a finitely
generated Λ-module. Then there is a pseudo-isomorphism (morphism with finite kernel and cokernel)
                                              𝑠                     𝑡
                                 𝑀 ∼ Λ𝑟 ⊕             Λ/ 𝑝 𝑎𝑖 Λ ⊕          Λ/ 𝑓𝑗 𝑗 Λ,

where 𝑟, 𝑠, 𝑡 ∈ ℤ ≥0 , 𝑎𝑖 ∈ ℤ ≥1 , and 𝑓𝑗 ∈ ℤ 𝑝 [ 𝛾 − 1] are distinguished irreducible polynomials
(Weierstrass polynomials). The invariants 𝑟 , 𝜇 ( 𝑀 ) = 𝑎𝑖 , 𝜆 ( 𝑀 ) = 𝑏𝑗 deg 𝑓𝑗 are well-defined.

Proof. Washington 1997 Introduction to Cyclotomic Fields Thm. 13.12; Coates–Sujatha 2006 §2.3. The
proof uses completeness of Λ with respect to 𝔪 = ( 𝑝, 𝛾 − 1) plus Weierstrass preparation.

Corollary 24.3.2 ( 𝜇 = 0 criterion). . 𝜇 ( 𝑀 ) = 0 iff 𝑀 has no Λ/ 𝑝 𝑎 Λ summand in its structure
theorem decomposition, iff the localization 𝑀( 𝑝 ) = 𝑀 ⊗Λ Λ ( 𝑝 ) (Noetherian localization at the prime

𝑟 = 0).
Proof. The summand Λ/ 𝑝 𝑎 Λ has ( 𝑝)-localization Λ ( 𝑝 ) / 𝑝 𝑎 Λ ( 𝑝 ) , which is non-zero iff 𝑎 ≥ 1. The
summand Λ/ 𝑓 𝑏 Λ has ( 𝑝)-localization zero because 𝑓 is a unit in Λ ( 𝑝 ) (distinguished 𝑓 ∈ ℤ 𝑝 [ 𝛾 − 1]
has non-zero constant term modulo 𝑝 ). The free part Λ𝑟 has full-rank ( 𝑝)-localization, which is zero-
dimensional over Frac(𝔽 𝑝 [[𝑇 ]]) iff 𝑟 = 0. Hence 𝜇 ( 𝑀 ) = 0 ⇔ no 𝑝-torsion summands, equivalently
( 𝑝)-localization is free over Λ ( 𝑝 ) (zero-dimensional over Frac(𝔽 𝑝 [[𝑇 ]]) precisely when 𝑟 = 0 as well).


Injective and Projective Resolutions Over Λ
Proposition 24.3.3 (injective resolution bound). . Every finitely generated Λ-module 𝑀 admits
an injective resolution 𝑀 → 𝐼 • with 𝐼 𝑘 = 0 for 𝑘 ≥ 3, where each 𝐼 𝑘 is a direct sum of injective hulls
of simple Λ-modules.

Proof. Λ is two-dimensional regular, hence has global injective dimension 2 (Serre 1963; Matsumura 1989
Thm. 18.1). The injective hulls are Λ∨ (Pontryagin dual of Λ), Λ∨ / 𝑝, and the residue field 𝔽 𝑝 regarded
as a Λ-module. Truncation at degree 2 gives the bound.

Proposition 24.3.4 (projective resolution bound). . Every finitely generated Λ-module 𝑀 admits
a projective resolution 𝑃 • → 𝑀 with 𝑃𝑘 = 0 for 𝑘 ≥ 3, where each 𝑃𝑘 is a finite direct sum of copies
of Λ.

Proof. Λ regular of dimension 2; Hilbert syzygy theorem gives the bound (Matsumura 1989 §18).

Proposition 24.3.5 (injective and projective resolutions cohere when 𝜇 = 0). . Let 𝑀 be a
finitely generated Λ-module with 𝜇 ( 𝑀 ) = 0. Then:

 (ii) The projective resolution 𝑃• of 𝑀 reduces modulo 𝑝 to a 𝔽 𝑝 [[𝑇 ]]-projective resolution of

Co-Derived and Contra-Derived Λ-Categories
Deﬁnition 24.3.6 (Λ-co-derived category). Let 𝐶 be an arithmetic dg Λ-coalgebra. The Λ-co-derived cate-
gory Dco
       Λ
         ( 𝐶 −comodΛ ) is the Verdier quotient of the homotopy category 𝐾 ( 𝐶 −comodΛ ) of complexes
of 𝐶 -comodules (which are naturally Λ-modules) by the class of complexes 𝑋 • such that:
  (i) 𝑋 • is homotopy equivalent to a complex of 𝐶 -injective Λ-modules, and
 (ii) 𝑋 • is acyclic in the sense of Positselski 2011 §3.5: Hom 𝐾 ( Λ ) (𝑌 , 𝑋 • ) = 0 for all 𝑌 in the subcate-
      gory of Λ-co-admissible complexes (bounded-below complexes of finitely generated Λ-comodules
      satisfying Nekovář’s admissibility).
Deﬁnition 24.3.7 (Λ-contra-derived category). Dually,the Λ-contra-derived category DctrΛ
                                                                                         ( 𝐶 ∨ −contramodΛ )
is the Verdier quotient of 𝐾 ( 𝐶 ∨ −contramodΛ ) by complexes that are both projective-homotopy-trivial
and Hom 𝐾 ( Λ ) ( 𝑋 • , 𝑌 ) = 0 for all 𝑌 in the subcategory of Λ-contra-admissible complexes (Greenberg
2001 §3).
Remark 24.3.8 (comparison with Nekovář). Nekovář 2006 §1.2 defines the Λ-derived category
D( Λ−Mod) through the abelian category of compact Λ-modules. The co-derived and contra-derived
categories above refine this by distinguishing injective-resolution direction from projective-resolution
direction; this distinction is invisible over a field (where injective = projective for finite-dimensional
vector spaces) but active over Λ.
Lemma 24.3.9 (representability of co- and contra-derived categories). . When 𝜇 ( 𝐶 ) = 0, both

Lurie HA 1.4.4, and the compact objects are precisely the finitely generated comodules (resp. contramod-

Proof. Presentability follows from Chapter 24.3.3 and Chapter 24.3.4: bounded injective / projective

24.4    The Main Theorem
Overview of the Proof
The proof of Chapter 24.1.5 proceeds in six steps:
   (i) (Construction of the pair of functors.) Define functors Ψ : Dco

  (ii) (Base-change to 𝔽 𝑝 [[𝑇 ]].) Reduce along Λ → 𝔽 𝑝 [[𝑇 ]] and apply the classical Positselski result
       over the one-dimensional valuation ring.
 (iii) (Lifting along Nakayama.) Use complete Noetherianity of Λ plus 𝜇 = 0 to lift the base-change
       equivalence to a Λ-equivalence.
 (iv) (Bar–cobar adjunction check.) Verify that ΩΛ ⊣ 𝐵 Λ factors through the equivalence.
  (v) (Unit / counit quasi-isomorphism.) Verify that the derived unit 𝐶 → ΩΛ 𝐵 Λ ( 𝐶 ) and counit
       𝐵 Λ ΩΛ ( 𝐴) → 𝐴 are quasi-isomorphisms under 𝜇 = 0.
 (vi) (Independence of tower presentation.) Check that the equivalence does not depend on the choice
       of Λ → 𝔽 𝑝 [[𝑇 ]] reduction.

Theorem 24.4.7 ( Λ -bar–cobar adjunction). . Let ΩΛ and 𝐵 Λ denote the bar and cobar functors on

Assembly: the Main Theorem
Proof of Chapter 24.1.5. Assemble Steps 1–6. Step 1 constructs the functor pair Ψ, Φ (Chapter 24.4.1,
Chapter 24.4.2). Step 2 reduces to 𝔽 𝑝 [[𝑇 ]] (Chapter 24.4.4) and applies Positselski 2018 for the classical
equivalence over the one-dimensional valuation ring. Step 3 lifts the equivalence along Nakayama

(Chapter 24.4.7). Step 5 verifies that the unit / counit are quasi-isomorphisms (Chapter 24.4.8). Step 6
shows the equivalence is independent of choices (Chapter 24.4.9).
   Combining: under 𝜇 ( 𝐶 ) = 0 (plus dual 𝜇-condition on the contramodule side), Ψ is an equivalence,
and the bar–cobar adjunction restricts to an adjoint pair inducing the equivalence between the co-derived
category of Λ-comodules and the contra-derived category of Λ-contramodules. This is Chapter 24.1.5.


Remark 24.4.10 (dual 𝜇-invariant condition). The hypothesis on the contramodule side is that the
Selmer 𝜇-invariant of the 𝐶 ∨ -contramodule tower vanishes. Under Iwasawa duality (Coates–Sujatha
2006 §3.1, Poitou–Tate arithmetic duality adapted to Iwasawa towers), the Selmer 𝜇-invariant equals
the classical 𝜇-invariant modulo pseudo-nullity. Hence under 𝜇 ( 𝐶 ) = 0 for the comodule side, the dual
Selmer 𝜇 condition is automatically satisfied for 𝐶 ∨ .

24.6    Archimedean Extension: Gaussian Positselski
The Archimedean Analogue
At the archimedean place, the base ring changes from Λ = ℤ 𝑝 [[ Γ]] to ℝ (or ℂ), and the Iwasawa
deformation becomes a Gaussian deformation of the Heisenberg Fock: the archimedean local factor is
H (∞) = ℂ[ 𝛼−1 , 𝛼−2 , . . .] · |0⟩∞ with Gaussian inner product (Segal 1981; Frenkel–Ben-Zvi 2004 §3.5).

Remark 24.6.3 (adelic functional equation as adelic Positselski). Under the adelic arithmetic Positselski
equivalence (Chapter 24.6.2), the functional equation 𝜉 ( 𝑠 ) = 𝜉 (1 − 𝑠 ) becomes an assertion about
the Fourier-invariance of the adelic bar–cobar pairing: 𝜉 ( 𝑠 ) is the Mellin transform of the adelic theta
distribution Θ, and Fourier invariance F𝔸 Θ = Θ gives 𝜉 ( 𝑠 ) = 𝜉 (1 − 𝑠 ). The arithmetic Positselski
equivalence is the categorical reflection of this Fourier self-duality; the functional equation is its character-
level shadow.

Prime Traces, Hall Operators, and Modular
Conjugation

The finite primary tower has one state of energy 𝑛 log 𝑝 at occupation 𝑛. Its character is an Euler factor.
To compare that tower with a Koszul or Petersson pairing, one must also specify its observables and
the functional which measures them. We construct those data, realize their creation operator on a Hall
sector, and determine the Hilbert space and modular conjugation of the resulting state. The distinction
between an occupation vector, a projection, and an algebra element controls every normalization in this
passage.

25.2    The full algebra of prime shifts
To determine exactly what the vacuum test excludes, we compute the algebra generated by 𝑆 and 𝑅.
All algebras and tensor products in the algebraic calculations are over ℂ, and all sums are finite unless
convergence is specified. The operators have cohomological degree zero. Their separate occupation
degrees are deg 𝑆 = 1 and deg 𝑅 = −1.
